messages.content: Why does a team often play better at its home ground?
Home teams have a few advantages. Because they know the ground well, have not had to travel, and hear their own supporters cheering, which can lift their confidence.
Why do clouds look grey before rain but white on a sunny day?
Rain clouds are thick and full of water. Because thick clouds block much of the sunlight passing through them, so their bottoms look dark grey, while thin clouds scatter light and look white.
Why does honey pour slowly while water pours fast?
Honey is much thicker. Because its tiny parts cling to each other and resist moving past one another, so it flows more slowly.
Why do rooms feel warmer when many people are inside?
Each person gives off heat. Because our bodies make warmth all the time, and in a closed room it adds up with nowhere to go.
Why do people sometimes talk loudly when they are excited?
They forget to control the volume. Because excitement fills them with energy and their attention is on the news, they stop noticing how loud they are.
Pooja drinks either tea or coffee in the morning. Today she did not drink tea. What did she drink?
She drank coffee. Because tea or coffee were the only two choices and tea is ruled out, coffee is what is left.
The road to the station is flooded. What is a wise plan?
Find another route or wait. Because floodwater can be deeper than it looks and may hide holes or strong currents, walking through it is risky.
Why does a cycle tyre become hard when we pump air into it?
Packed-in air pushes harder on the rubber. Because more and more air is squeezed into the same space, its push on the inside of the rubber grows and the tyre stiffens.
Why does water roll off a duck's back instead of soaking in?
The feathers are oily. Because the oil makes the feathers repel water, the duck's body stays dry and warm even when it swims.
Why does wet mud turn hard and crack under the hot sun?
The water in the mud dries away. Because the tiny clay grains stick tightly together as the water leaves and the mud shrinks, the ground splits into cracks.
How does a mosquito net protect a sleeping person?
The net protects by keeping mosquitoes away. Because its tiny holes are too small for the insects to pass through, they cannot reach the skin to bite.
Why do we feel no pain when we trim the ends of our fingernails?
The hard tip of the nail has no feeling, so trimming does not hurt. Because the nerves lie in the skin underneath and not in the hard nail itself, the cut ends are like dry hair.
Why does a shirt look darker when it is wet?

A wet shirt sends less light back to our eyes. Because water fills the tiny gaps between the threads and lets more of the light pass into the cloth instead of bouncing off it, less reflected light reaches us.
Some fruits are sweet, and a lemon is a fruit. Is a lemon sweet?
We cannot be sure from this alone. Because the first sentence says only that some fruits are sweet, it does not tell us which ones, so it cannot settle the question about a lemon.
Why should a group agree on a meeting place before going to a crowded fair?
A meeting place helps people who get separated. Because a crowd makes it easy to lose each other, and phones may not work in the noise, everyone knows where to go to find the others.
Why should a pot on the stove never be left alone for long?

Things can go wrong quickly on a stove, so someone should stay nearby. Because food can boil over onto the flame or boil dry and burn, and a fire can start when nobody is there to stop it, a pot should not be left alone.
Why does a plant on a sunny window sill dry out faster than a plant in a shady corner?
Sun and moving air pull water out of the window plant's soil and leaves more quickly. Because warmth makes water leave faster, the plant in sunshine needs water sooner.
What number added to 14 makes 30?
How many eggs are there in 12 dozen?
144. Because 1 dozen is 12, so 12 x 12 = 144, which is 12 dozen.
Double 59 is what?
118. Because double means two times, and 59 x 2 = 118.
